mechanism: Smooth Standard Deviation into a histogram with three empirical thresholds (FlatLevel, MiddleTrendLevel, MaxTrendLevel). Classify the bar as flat / medium trend / strong trend by which band StdDev occupies; Used Trend input selects which band is tradable. Confirmed by ColorZerolagRVI cloud color for direction.
data_needed: Close (or applied price) series; StdDev smoothing period and EMA method; calibrated Flat/Middle/Max levels
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; H1 (H4 cited for strong-trend mode); test window 2016.01.01–2017.03.01
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit three-state volatility-of-returns regime tag (flat/medium/strong) already wired to a confirmation oscillator, reusable as a sleeve gate.
quote: The ColorStdDev histogram is red (a strong trend) … Flat level … Middle trend level … Maximum trend level

mechanism: Build a fan of Total MAs starting at StartPeriod with Step increments; on each bar count how many MAs sit above vs below Close and emit histogram = tot_Bid − tot_Ask. Positive fan consensus marks bullish momentum regime, negative marks bearish; used with Average Change crossing 1 for entries.
data_needed: Close series; StartPeriod, Step, Total, MA type/price
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H4 (strategy #10); same 2016–2017 EURUSD test set
why_new_for_mis: Turns a multi-period MA consensus count into a compact signed regime score MIS can stream without committing to a single MA period.
quote: The value of the histogram shows the difference between the number of MAs above and below the close price

mechanism: On a rolling Sample of bars, compute average High/Low deviations at 25/50/75% and max; trade when Close breaks the 75% growth/reduction quartile while Weight Oscillator is rising/falling. The 75% quartile is an empirical amplitude envelope—breakout beyond typical excursion marks an elevated-volatility expansion.
data_needed: OHLC; Sample length; quartile percents (25/50/75); Weight Oscillator (RSI/MFI/WPR/DeMarker)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; strategy #6 in the 10-strategy suite
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a non-parametric amplitude envelope (empirical quartiles of bar excursion) as a volatility/expansion sensor, distinct from ATR/StdDev.
quote: Quartile 3 corresponds to the average value of price reduction … in 75% of cases. It is used in our strategy.

idea_name: Donchian CLOSE_HIGH_LOW channel as spike-robust volatility band
mechanism: Donchian upper/lower = max/min over DonchianPeriod of a chosen extrema type. CLOSE_HIGH_LOW uses highest/lowest Close (not High/Low), so long wick spikes do not inflate the band—channel width then tracks sustained range rather than noise. Breakouts of this band are the volatility-expansion events; author notes classical High/Low is distorted by EURUSD shadows.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD and GOLD-6.17; M30–H1 best (not D1); 2016.03.01–2017.03.01; every-tick real ticks
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a wick-resistant range/volatility envelope whose width and breakouts are cleaner regime tags than classical Donchian on noisy FX.
quote: close prices tend to be more objective … spikes distort channel borders, while close prices tend to be more objective.

mechanism: Average Speed indicator measures mean price change in points/min over Inp_Bars; require Average Speed > Trend_lev (e.g. 1–2) plus multi-RSI semaphore confirmation before accepting a Donchian breakout. Filters false breakouts when price is moving too slowly to sustain the expansion.
data_needed: Close (or applied price); bar count; Trend_lev threshold; optional X4Period_RSI_Arrows
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 Donchian+AvrSpeed+RSI tandem; GOLD-6.17 noted as too selective under low futures vol
why_new_for_mis: Adds a rate-of-change (points/min) liveliness sensor MIS can use to gate breakout/expansion signals when the tape is stagnant.
quote: The value of Average Speed must be greater than 1, and the semaphore RSI must mark at least 2 points

mechanism: For each of five detectors (ADX>TrendLevel; ColorBBCandles non-zero; Percentage-of-Trend outside Up/Dn levels; RSIFilter hist=1; ZigZagTrendDetector hist=1) count bars in trend over NumCandles and report (count/N)*100 on M1…W1. Average across methods ≈60% trend time under the article’s settings—explicit trend-vs-flat occupancy sensor per symbol/TF.
data_needed: OHLC per TF; ADX/BB/PoT/RSI/ZZ params; NumCandles sample (2000 default)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, USDCHF, USDJPY, GBPUSD, GOLD-6.17, #MCD; M1–W1; 2000-bar samples
why_new_for_mis: Delivers a multi-detector, multi-TF trend-occupancy panel MIS can use as a regime prior (how much of recent history is trending vs flat).
quote: the average market value in the trend state is about 60%, while on the time scale from the past to the present the trend/flat ratio shifts toward the flat

mechanism: Measure average trend-time % at sample sizes X∈{100,200,300,500,1000,1500,2000}, rank-correlate with Spearman ρ against X. Strong positive ρ means deeper history was more trending (edge migrating toward flat today); near-zero ρ means stable character; negative ρ means recent bars are more trending. Validates on weekly charts (EURUSD 1995–2017, USDJPY, #MCD).
data_needed: Same trend detectors; multiple sample depths; Spearman critical-value table
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/USDCHF/USDJPY/GBPUSD/GOLD-6.17/#MCD; coefficient tables per method; weekly visual audit
why_new_for_mis: Turns the dependence of trend occupancy on lookback depth into a change sensor for secular shifts in market character—MIS can watch ρ and trend% drift as a slow regime-break flag.
quote: the trend/flat ratio has shifted towards the sideways movements; earlier the trend was more visible and obvious than it is today.

mechanism: Embed WFO meta-params (window W days, step S as % of W, stepOffset) into tester optimization; score in-sample only via OnTester custom criterion, stash out-of-sample step results. Cluster report grids Annualized profit, Efficiency (test/opt annual profit ratio), Consistency (% profitable forward steps). Cells with Consistency>50% and high Efficiency mark W/S regimes where the EA’s edge persists—collapse of Consistency across adjacent cells flags parameter/regime fragility.
data_needed: EA with WFO library hooks; custom OnTester; CSV/HTML WFO report; fixed-lot strategies
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 demo EA (Envelopes+WPR); D≈2015.01–2017.06; W custom 90–180d, S 10–30%
why_new_for_mis: Frames rolling/cluster forward Consistency and Efficiency as sensors of whether a strategy’s edge is stationary across time windows—MIS can treat Consistency drops as regime-change alarms for live sleeves.
quote: Consistency is a percentage of profitable passes among all test passes of the combined forward. … recommended to have a consistency above 50%.

mechanism: TradeObjects EA maps chart object color/style/width/prefix to alerts, market/pending orders, and closes, with EventHotSpot/EventTimeSpan debounce. Semi-automatic markup executor—no market sensing built.

why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—chart-object trade automation UI only.

mechanism: Fit OLS linear regression of cumulative trade balance vs trade index via ALGLIB; TrendProfit = regression rise per trade; TrendMSE = m_rmserror; ProfitStability = (TrendProfit/TrendMSE) × n_trades [/ total_volume]. Custom OnTester max favors steep, smooth equity—penalizes jagged paths that often coincide with regime-mismatched trading. Forward tests with volume normalization sometimes surfaced only negative OOS, i.e. more realistic fragility.
data_needed: Deal history (commission+swap+profit); start balance; optional volume normalization flag
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H4 and M15; Wizard FixedRisk EA, Moving Average, MACD Sample; with/without forward
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an equity-path smoothness/steepness sensor (regression slope over residual RMSE) usable as a live sleeve-health gauge when the balance path turns jagged under the same rules.
quote: ProfitStability is calculated as a ratio of TrendProfit to LR Standard error

mechanism: Parse tester HTML deals; at each open time snapshot indicator level and dynamics (=value_t/value_{t-1}) for ATR, CCI, StdDev, Volumes, Force, Chaikin, BW MFI, MACD, ADX, Alligator; bin by value×dynamics×direction and sum PnL into HTML charts. Profitable bins become entry filters (e.g. CCI>200 rising for buys; MACD Signal above histogram for buys)—empirical map from indicator state space to edge regime.
data_needed: Tester HTML report in Common Files; indicator handles/params; deal tickets/times/PnL

mechanism: Define BUY trend when LIPS>TEETH>JAW, SELL when LIPS<TEETH<JAW, else FLAT/indefinite. Combine with per-line dynamics (DiffLips/Teeth/Jaw = MA_t/MA_{t-1}) to gate Kalman signals—e.g. buy on sell-trend if LIPS or JAW turns up; buy on buy-trend if LIPS and TEETH rise; buy on flat if TEETH and JAW fall. Explicit three-state geometric regime from MA stack order.
data_needed: Three SMMA (Jaw/Teeth/Lips) with periods/shifts; ratio dynamics per line
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD H1 Kalman EA; Alligator defaults 13/8, 8/5, 5/3 SMMA median
why_new_for_mis: Hands MIS a simple ordinal MA-stack regime (trend-up / trend-down / flat) plus line-turn dynamics, shown to lift PF 0.75→1.12 when used as a filter.
quote: If LIPS line is higher than TEETH, while TEETH is higher than JAW — consider BUY as a trend. … In case of absence of a strict order of lines consider the trend as indefinite or FLAT.

mechanism: Boltzmann/Cauchy/ultrafast annealing classes drive EA parameter search inside the tester with temperature schedules and a frame GUI. Stochastic optimizer competing with GA—no market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—parameter-search algorithm only.
quote: Simulated annealing is one of the methods of stochastic optimization.

mechanism: Treat each historical trade’s relative profit k=C1/C0 as i.i.d. draws from the empirical F; resample NSAMPLES paths of length n (bootstrap). Optimization criteria mean_sd = E[final profit]/SD and med_intq = median / IQR prefer high mean profit with low path scatter—explicit robustness-to-random-reorder sensor of the trade distribution.
data_needed: Closed-deal relative profits; NSAMPLES; optional rmndmin for drawdown-capped paths
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 Moving Average_mcarlo; spring/summer 2017; OHLC M1 modeling
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS bootstrap-based profit-stability scores (mean/SD, median/IQR) as sleeve-health sensors: rising scatter of resampled terminal wealth flags fragile edge under trade-order noise.
quote: Our criterion will be equal to the ratio of the average profit to its average scatter. It is similar to the Sharpe ratio.

mechanism: Split the trade-profit sequence into early and late subsamples (fwdsh fraction); compute WMW U-statistic and map to 1−|1−2U/(nkf·nkp)| so equal distributions score near 1 and shifts score near 0. High WMW supports stationary trade PnL (Monte Carlo assumptions hold); collapse marks non-stationarity of the profit distribution—i.e. a regime break in the EA’s edge even if prices alone look similar.
data_needed: Ordered trade relative-profit series; fwdsh∈(0,1); min deals per half
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD H1 MA EA window; frw_wmw and frw_wmw_prf criteria
why_new_for_mis: Directly senses change in the trade-result distribution (not just price)—MIS can run WMW on live sleeve PnL halves as an early warning that the edge’s law has shifted.
quote: a criterion measuring the stability of profit in terms of the persistence of the trade profits distribution. … stationarity of trade profits
